 Ford Recalls 330 Bronco SUVs Over Wipers That Can Fall Off
 by 
 TTAC News Staff 
 (IC: ) 
 Published:  November 13th, 2026 
 Share 
 Ford recalled 330 examples of the 2026 Bronco because the driver-side windshield wipers can detach from the vehicle. The culprit is a wiper arm nut that may loosen, leaving the blade to part ways with the SUV.
 Enjoy our posts? 
 Add TheTruthAboutCars as a Preferred Source on Google 
 According to the National Highway Transportation Safety Administration (NHTSA) report , a loose nut on the driver-side wiper arm can let the wiper detach entirely. Lose the driver-side wiper, and you lose visibility in rain or snow, which is where a wiper is supposed to earn its keep. NHTSA's consequence language is blunt about the stakes: reduced driver visibility in certain weather conditions "increasing the risk of a crash."
 For a vehicle whose entire marketing pitch is conquering the great outdoors, a wiper that bails in bad weather is an awkward look. The good news, if there is any, is the scope. At 330 units, this is a small campaign, the kind of number that suggests an isolated assembly or supplier issue rather than a fleet-wide defect.
 Dealers will check the wipers, snug up the arm nut, and swap in new wiper arms if needed, at no cost to the owner, according to NHTSA. Nothing here requires new electronics or a software patch, just a wrench and, where needed, fresh hardware.
 The report was received Nov. 2. VINs tied to the recall could be looked up on NHTSA.gov starting Nov. 6, so owners who want to know their status now have a way to check. Owner notification letters are expected to go out Nov. 16.
 Owners with questions can reach Ford customer service at 1-866-436-7332 and reference Ford's recall number, 26S82, or NHTSA campaign 26V725000. Anyone who wants to confirm whether a specific truck is affected can run the VIN through the NHTSA site rather than wait for the mailer.
 It's a minor recall by the numbers, but a wiper detaching mid-storm is exactly the kind of failure that turns a nuisance into a liability. Cheap to fix, worth fixing promptly.
